artists.biography: Sleep is a stoner doom metal band from San Jose, California. Active during the 1990s, Sleep earned critical and record label attention early in their career. Critic Eduardo Rivadavia describes them as "perhaps the ultimate stoner rock band"and notes they exerted a strong influence on heavy metal in the 1990s. However, conflict with their record company had contributed to Sleep's breakup by the end of the decade. The band reformed, performing sporadic live dates, in 2009.

Sleep.biography: Sleep is a stoner doom metal band from San Jose, California. Active during the 1990s, Sleep earned critical and record label attention early in their career. Critic Eduardo Rivadavia describes them as "perhaps the ultimate stoner rock band"and notes they exerted a strong influence on heavy metal in the 1990s. However, conflict with their record company had contributed to Sleep's breakup by the end of the decade. The band reformed, performing sporadic live dates, in 2009.

apple_music.editorial_notes: Stoner metal fans worldwide felt a seismic shift in the wake of Sleep’s 2026 lineup reconfiguration. Though some lamented the departures of co-founder Matt Pike and reunion-era drummer Jason Roeder, low-end shaman Al Cisneros forges ahead, leading a redoubtable new trio poised to bring the band into its next era. Beginning with the heady cosmic jam “Have Spacesuit Will Travel”, Hempispheres [sic] showcases the talents of freshly installed members Dale Crover and Bubba Dupree, whose respective experiences with groups like Melvins and Void unlock unheard facets of the group’s potential. Serving as the album’s celestial centrepiece, the title track accentuates its splendid sprawl with tight rhythmic curves and hazy riffage. Traces of Cisneros and Crover’s work together in short-lived supergroup Shrinebuilder seep through on the doomy groove of “The Morrisist”, while Dupree’s bluesy tendencies add sinew to girthy Frankensteined closer “Whole Wheat Mountain / Well Baked”. Our Favourite Track: While certainly not as monumental as Sleep’s hourlong tour de force “Dopesmoker”, the 11-minute “Arrival of the Industry Ships” reveals the new ensemble’s innate propensity for cannabis-inspired sci-fi sagas.
apple_music.name: Hempispheres

editorialNotes.short: Al Cisneros leads a new lineup deeper into the cosmic haze.

lastfm.wiki_content: Hempispheres is the fifth studio album by the American stoner doom metal band Sleep. The album was digitally released on September 3, 2026, with physical copies set to be released on October 30, 2026, through Third Man Records. The album was preceded by the single "Have Spacesuit Will Travel (4:20 Flexi Edit)" that was released in June 2026 alongside a comic book written by Al Cisneros and illustrated by Dave Kloc and Arik Roper. The album marks the first release of Sleep's new formation, consisting of vocalist Al Cisneros, guitarist Bubba Dupree and drummer Dale Crover, replacing Matt Pike and Jason Roeder. Musically, the album maintains a reverence for Black Sabbath and Tony Iommi, while drawing on sonic traits evocative of acid blues and proto-metal from bands such as Cactus, Deep Purple and Hawkwind. perplexity.description:
Hempispheres is a 2026 studio album by Sleep, released through Third Man Records. Across five extended tracks, the band stretches its stoner-doom vocabulary into hazy space-rock territory, pairing downtuned, deliberate riffs with Al Cisneros’s hypnotic bass and vocals. Songs such as “Have Spacesuit Will Travel,” “Hempispheres,” and the 11-minute “Arrival of the Industry Ships” emphasize cosmic imagery, repetition, and gradual rhythmic development rather than conventional verse-chorus structures.

The album also marks a new phase in Sleep’s lineup, with drummer Dale Crover and guitarist Bubba Dupree bringing links to the Melvins, Void, and Washington, D.C.’s punk underground. Their contributions add sharper rhythmic turns, blues-inflected guitar color, and a slightly more exploratory edge to the group’s famously monolithic sound. Hempispheres retains Sleep’s ritualistic heaviness while presenting a comparatively concise, tightly focused collection, issued digitally in September 2026 and physically by Third Man Records the following month.
